recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Further named-product examples would be optional editorial work for BR&R rather than a necessary current-spec correction.
issue_request: FHIR-31820 was a Published/Persuasive BR&R FHIR-core issue for MedicinalProductIngredient asking whether both strength and referenceStrength make sense, with a resolution to improve documentation, call out that the reference substance must also be specified, and provide examples.
initial_application: No current-source commit explicitly tagged FHIR#31820 was found. The companion FHIR#31819 commits 72c7bcfe69c0b11deaefc688b833b242cf18474c and 9ac982b98acc0b1b67fdc1dd53c4b087e29419f7 added the definition text quoted in the FHIR-31820 comments, and the active Ingredient example already shows a strength with referenceStrength.
additional_context: MedicinalProductIngredient now redirects to the active Ingredient resource. FHIR-35931 later made Ingredient.substance.strength.referenceStrength.substance 1..1, so the model requires the reference substance whenever referenceStrength is used. Community searches found no direct conflicting discussion; the Confluence hit only listed FHIR-31820 with other BR&R R4B ballot work, and a later Zulip thread was consistent with the current model.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current StructureDefinition says both a strength and a reference strength are needed in the active substance versus active moiety case, referenceStrength.substance is mandatory, and the example demonstrates both values together.
